notes: Daniel's top priority is #1 (response/resolution trend, and variance by merchant), so I'm spending 2 of tonight's 3 slots there: a platform-wide monthly trend (to see direction of travel) and a per-merchant snapshot for the latest full year (to see spread across merchants, since he likes peer comparisons). The third slot starts #2 (where load comes from) with a tag-based mix comparing the last two half-years to catch any shift. I'm deliberately holding off on YoY columns inside the trend report itself since the 36-month series already shows year-over-year pattern, and saving width for the core time metrics. Returns/refunds (#3), satisfaction (#4) and reviews (#5) are next on my list for later nights.

requests.title: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
requests.question: Is first-response and resolution speed on support tickets getting better or worse over time?
requests.grain: one calendar month, platform-wide across all tenants
requests.details: Source: tickets, joined to sla_breaches for breach rate. Grain the month on tickets.created_at (date_trunc to month / use calendar_days.month_label for the label). Window: 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (full history, 36 rows). First response hours = extract(epoch from first_response_at - created_at)/3600, only for tickets where first_response_at is not null (report both the count with a response and the avg/median so the denominator is clear). Resolution hours = extract(epoch from resolved_at - created_at)/3600 for tickets where resolved_at is not null. SLA breach rate = distinct tickets in that month's cohort with at least one row in sla_breaches, divided by tickets created that month, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal. Round all hour figures to 1 decimal. Note in the report how many of the 36 months are returned, and flag that the most recent 1-2 months will understate resolution/response times for tickets still open (right-censoring) so we read the tail with caution. Order by month ascending.

requests.title: Response & resolution times by merchant, 2025
requests.question: How much does support speed vary across merchants, and who is fastest/slowest?
requests.grain: one row per tenant (merchant), for tickets created in 2025
requests.details: Source: tickets joined to tenants (for name) and sla_breaches (for breach rate). Filter tickets.created_at in 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. Same hour definitions as the monthly trend report (first_response_at - created_at, resolved_at - created_at, both in hours, only over tickets where that timestamp is not null). SLA breach rate = tenant's distinct tickets with >=1 sla_breaches row / tenant's tickets created in 2025, as a percentage. Only include tenants with at least 20 tickets created in 2025 to avoid noisy small-sample rows. Order by tickets created descending, tie-break by merchant name ascending; report will show at most 50 rows so note total tenant count meeting the threshold and how many are printed.
builds_on: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly

requests.title: Ticket topic mix and recent shift
requests.question: What kinds of problems are shoppers contacting merchants about most, and has that mix shifted in the last 6 months versus the prior 6?
requests.grain: one row per support tag (platform-wide, tag name)
requests.details: Source: tickets joined to ticket_tags_map and support_tags (group by support_tags.name across all tenants, since we want the platform-level theme). A ticket can carry multiple tags; count each ticket once per tag it carries (so a ticket with 2 tags contributes to both tag rows - note this in the report so totals don't have to sum to ticket volume). Period A = tickets.created_at between 2025-07-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive; period B = 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30 inclusive. Share of tickets = tag's ticket count in that period / total tagged-ticket-tag-rows in that period, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal. Share change = share in period A minus share in period B, in percentage points, rounded to 1 decimal. avg resolution hours (period A only) = extract(epoch from resolved_at - created_at)/3600 averaged over that tag's resolved tickets in period A, rounded to 1 decimal. Order by tickets in the last 6 months descending, tie-break by tag name ascending. Report total distinct tag count returned (expect well under 50 rows).
